endorsements.quote: Once an application is developed and deployed, a pilot program would help validate the application and its clinical value.

While any successful adoption requires seamless integration with existing EHR systems, a pilot program could benefit from a quick but usable de-novo front-end before investing into further EHR integration.
When this is suspected, the data scientist should investigate if the new population is different from the training population and consider re-training the model.

unlisted_practices: Identify an operational home responsible for uptime and maintenance of the deployed model before or during the pilot.
Treat information security and required committee approvals as a longitudinal consideration throughout deployment, and capture only the minimum necessary data at each stage.
Write unit tests for pre-processing and post-processing modules and maintain validation datasets to detect changes in model accuracy.
Build logging, debuggability, and documentation into deployed ML code.
Articulate the clinical value proposition of a model and align it with organizational priorities before deployment.
Ensure necessary data inputs are available at or before the time the prediction is needed.
Engage clinician end-users, data scientists, PI, and IT engineers in inverted-ETL requirements gathering, working backwards from desired outputs to data sources.
Create interface mock-ups with end-user input before building the application.
Watch for lost data connections and changes in data structure after deployment.
Monitor for workflow or clinical practice changes that conflict with the model and adjust the model accordingly.

screen.reason: This is an operational guidance/framework article proposing a strategy and defining stakeholder roles for deploying clinical machine learning tools in academic medical centers.
